book.title: Blue Ocean Strategy
book.author: W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne

confidence_note: Canvas definition is from the authors' site (high). Southwest details (dropped meals, seat choice, hub connectivity; kept friendly service, speed, frequent point-to-point departures; the car comparison and tagline) come from secondary summaries and are medium. The old text's 'most companies are surprised' claim and unverified lists (business class, lounges) were dropped.
facts: The strategy canvas has the factors an industry competes and invests in along the horizontal axis and the level buyers receive on each along the vertical axis.
Plotting rivals shows how similar their strategies look to buyers, which signals a red ocean.
Rival airlines invested across many factors.
Southwest dropped or cut meals, seat choice and hub connectivity and concentrated on friendly service, speed and frequent point-to-point departures at a low price.
The authors set car travel on the canvas as a comparison.
Southwest attracted car drivers by making flying more like driving; a tagline cited: 'The speed of the plane at the price of the car, whenever you need it.'
scene_details: a line plotted across factors such as meals, seat choice, speed
car travel drawn on the same chart as flights
frequent departures between pairs of cities
tension: Everyone's line on the chart looks the same, and one airline picks the car as its rival.
opening_idea: Open with the chart and the extra line the authors draw for the car.

lessons.idea: Putting your offer on the same chart as your rivals shows whether you are different or only similar.
lessons.anchor: Southwest's line against the other airlines' and the car.

reflect_final: If you drew your offer and your closest rival's on one chart, which two or three factors would the lines separate on?

use_cases.situation: Strategy discussion where everyone repeats the same selling points
use_cases.move: Say: let's plot us and the two closest rivals on factors. Southwest cut most of them and kept three.

use_cases.situation: Choosing how to stand out in a job search
use_cases.move: List what every candidate shows, then choose two things you will do differently.

use_cases.situation: A friend's café looks like every other café
use_cases.move: Ask: what do customers choose you for that the café next door cannot say?

pocket_idea: Southwest drew the car on the airline chart and kept only the factors a driver cares about: plot yourself before you compete.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Southwest picked the car as its competitor and cut most of what other airlines offered.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Airlines plotted on a chart look alike; Southwest cut meals and seat choice, kept friendly service, speed and frequent departures at a low price, and drew car drivers.
